key_insight: The AI co-mathematician is a stateful, agentic workbench that accelerates mathematical research by orchestrating specialized AI agents across ideation, literature search, computation and theorem proving, while managing uncertainty and failed hypotheses.
problem_solved: Addresses the fragmented, iterative and exploratory nature of mathematical research by providing an asynchronous workspace that refines user intent, records hypotheses and coordinates agentic tools to make open-ended discovery practical and reproducible.
method: Provide a stateful, asynchronous workspace that captures work history, failed hypotheses and evolving user intent.
Orchestrate specialized agents for ideation, literature search, symbolic/numeric computation and theorem proving into a single iterative loop.
Integrate uncertainty management and refinement mechanisms so agents propose, test and refine conjectures collaboratively with the human researcher.
impact: Makes human–AI collaboration in mathematics more productive and reproducible, reducing iteration time on discovery tasks and enabling practitioners to scale exploratory research workflows with agentic systems.
visual_elements: Workflow loop diagram showing human ↔ multi-agent interactions (ideation → search → compute → prove → refine).
UI mockup of the stateful workspace/timeline that tracks hypotheses, tests and failed attempts.
Icon set representing agent types (ideation, literature search, computation, theorem prover) and how they connect.
Before/after bar or timeline chart illustrating reduced iteration count or time-to-insight on example tasks.
paper_title: AI Co-Mathematician: Accelerating Mathematicians with Agentic AI
paper_authors: Daniel Zheng, Ingrid von Glehn, Yori Zwols, Iuliya Beloshapka, Lars Buesing
